author: RosieCampbell
text:
4. Accreditation alternatives to full publication are essential for limited disclosure.

In cybersecurity & in science, the first discoverer gets all the prestige. But there might be occasions where it's prudent to delay publishing. We need a way to allocate credit appropriately.

author: RosieCampbell
text:
3. Institutional support is required for a systematic, full-stack approach to safety.

Bug bounties are an interesting mechanism that we might want to consider for AI. But without institutional support and resources, it may be precarious to rely on them.

author: RosieCampbell
text:
2. Collaboration is effective and possible, if legal issues are anticipated.

Despite working at competing companies, the turning point was getting people in a room together to solve the problem.

"Getting to be engineers together in person was amazing" - Matt Linton

author: RosieCampbell
text:
1. Developing coordination policies proactively is essential.

Had Spectre or Meltdown been discovered just a decade earlier, the coordination policy would not have existed. AI vulnerabilities may also be harder to “patch” than traditional bugs. We need to work on policies now.

author: RosieCampbell
text: Very pleased to share our second case study on responsible publication norms - thank you @j_asminewang and @hudsonhongo for your hard work! This one was a fascinating story. Here's some stuff we learned 👇

quoted.text: The AI community has just started to grapple with the public risks associated with the publication of high-stakes research. By studying the Meltdown and Spectre case, we can learn how thoughtful norms played out after a real-life sensitive discovery. https://t.co/HMTU3HdcOX
